title: Dinesh Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta and Dinesh Pathak, JJ.
disposition: Final assessment of 10.01.2022 quashed; fresh order after Clause 8.1(b)(iii) compliance.
headnote: The Division Bench quashed a 10 January 2022 final theft assessment because the provisional assessment, received on 5 January 2022, had not allowed the fifteen days Clause 8.1(b)(iii) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires to reply, and no personal-hearing date had been intimated. On the Corporation’s concession, the assessing officer was left free to pass a fresh order in accordance with those provisions.
facts: Dinesh Kumar Yadav challenged respondent no. 2’s order dated 10 January 2022, which had finalized a provisional assessment of 23 November 2021 under the Electricity Act, 2003. Counsel submitted that the provisional assessment was dispatched on 20 December 2021 and received only on 5 January 2022, so the petitioner was not given the fifteen days Clause 8.1(b)(iii) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires to file a reply, nor a date for personal hearing, before the final assessment.

holding_units.holding: A final assessment cannot stand where the provisional assessment/show-cause was served so late that the consumer did not get at least fifteen days under Clause 8.1(b)(iii) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to file a reply, and no date for personal hearing was intimated. The final order is liable to be quashed, with liberty to the assessing officer to pass a fresh order after complying with those requirements.

principle_tags.application: Provisional assessment dispatched 20.12.2021 and received 05.01.2022 did not give fifteen days to reply before the 10.01.2022 final order; that order was quashed.
No date for personal hearing was intimated before the final theft assessment; the Corporation conceded a fresh order after that statutory step, and the Court quashed.

not_decided.point: Merits and quantum of the theft assessment
not_decided.note: The 10.01.2022 final order was quashed only for Clause 8.1(b)(iii) notice and hearing defects; respondent no. 2 was left free to pass a fresh order in accordance with law.
